content.thinking: I noticed a stripping bug: in phrases like "5 and 7 Series," only "7 Series" gets excluded, leaving the bare "5" misread as a data number. I'll fix the strip pattern to handle series lists, then test it against a realistic 13-claim brief.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("bmw_feedback/agents/verifier.py"); s = p.read_text()
a = '''         r"\\b[157]\\s?Series\\b", r"\\b(?:F70|G60|G68|G70|i5|i7|M60|M70)\\b",'''
b = '''         r"\\b[157](?:\\s*(?:,|and|&|/|or)\\s*[157])*\\s?Series\\b",      # '5 Series', '5 and 7 Series', '1, 5 and 7 Series'
         r"\\b(?:F70|G60|G68|G70|i5|i7|M60|M70)\\b",'''
assert s.count(a) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(a, b)); print("ok")
EOF
env -u OPENAI_API_KEY python3 - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tail -30
from bmw_feedback.decision import DecisionEngine
from bmw_feedback.agents.pipeline import Pipeline
from bmw_feedback.agents.contracts import Claim
from bmw_feedback.agents.verifier import rule_checks
p = Pipeline(DecisionEngine(), llm=None)
spec = {"idea": "head-up display that works with polarised sunglasses", "summary": "HUD", "move": "unspecified", "novelty": "matches_existing",
        "features": [{"feature": "Head-Up Display", "node_id": "feature:Head-Up Display", "reason": "t"}]}
e = p.evaluate(spec); idx = p._evals[e["evaluation_id"]]["bundle"].index()
brief = [
 ("Head-Up Display is a 'Consider' in Europe for the 5 and 7 Series and a 'Low priority' in the United States; customers like it, so the case is about usability, not demand.", ["f1.counts.consider", "f1.counts.low_priority", "f1.overall.verdict", "f1.overall.bad_kind"]),
 ("Customers rate it 'Leaning good' overall, with about 25% fewer complaints than expected (index 0.75, 65 comments).", ["f1.overall.verdict", "f1.overall.complaint_index"]),
 ("Most complaints are about usability: 20 difficult-to-use mentions versus 6 defects, led by 'hard to use / confusing' (18 comments).", ["f1.overall.bad_kind", "f1.reasons.negative"]),
 ("A US 5 Series customer called it \"overly busy, even when switched to the reduced setting\".", ["f1.G60.US.quote1"]),
 ("In Europe the 5 Series sells 115k units a year and scores 0.42 ('Consider'), but only 2 local comments exist, so the verdict is borrowed.", ["f1.G60.EU.volume", "f1.G60.EU.recommendation", "f1.G60.EU.complaints"]),
 ("In the US both the 5 and 7 Series are 'Low priority' (scores 0.22 and 0.26).", ["f1.G60.US.recommendation", "f1.G70.US.recommendation"]),
 ("US buyers rank the head-up display 24th of 103 attributes on the 5 Series (59.9% top-2 box).", ["f1.G60.US.survey1"]),
 ("On the 5 Series it is only available in the INNOVATIONSPAKET, from EUR 2,400 in Germany.", ["f1.price.G60"]),
 ("Prices are German list prices only; there is no US or China price list in the data.", ["caveat.prices-de-only"]),
 ("Nothing is known about Chinese customers: none of the 10,128 comments come from China.", ["caveat.no-china-feedback"]),
 ("Run a usability test of the HUD layout with 5 Series owners in Europe before changing its price.", ["f1.overall.bad_kind", "f1.G60.EU.recommendation"]),
 ("Evidence covers about 56% of sales volume; the rest has too little data for a recommendation.", ["f1.rollup.volume_share"]),
 ("The volume-weighted priority is 0.34 overall, closer to no case than a strong one.", ["f1.rollup.score"]),
]
bad = 0
for text, ids in brief:
    checks = rule_checks(Claim(id="c", section="s", text=text, fact_ids=ids), idx)
    failed = [f"{c.name}: {c.detail}" for c in checks if not c.passed]
    bad += bool(failed)
    print("OK  " if not failed else "FAIL", text[:80], failed)
print("over-stripped:", bad, "of", len(brief))
EOF

content.text:
I've built all of it: the knowledge graph, the three agents and the new single-page frontend. The agents have only been tested against a scripted stand-in for OpenAI, never against the real API. One thing will probably fail once you add your key: `gpt-6-terra` isn't in the OpenAI SDK's model list (the closest names are `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`). The explanation agent will most likely stop with "model unavailable" until you set `OPENAI_EXPLAINER_MODEL` to a model your account has. The app never swaps in a different model on its own.

**What you get**
- **Knowledge graph:** 15,064 nodes and 57,756 edges. It links feedback, features, reasons, the customer surveys, sales volumes, price-list items, fitment per variant and powertrain, technical specs and the trained models' outputs. Every node records where it came from (table, PDF page or model file). The build checks 23 counts against the source tables and stops on any mismatch. Four things are left out on purpose (dashboard re-exports, figure statistics and model internals among them); they're listed in the graph's schema file.
- **Agent 1 (retriever, `gpt-6-luna`):** finds candidate features with code only (names, aliases, the trained classifier, a search over the graph). The model may only choose among those. Its answer is checked with Pydantic and sent back with the errors if invalid. You confirm or edit what it extracted before anything is evaluated.
- **Decision engine (no LLM):** computes every number and turns it into facts, each with an ID and a pointer to its source.
- **Agent 2 (explainer, `gpt-6-terra`):** writes the brief for product managers. Every sentence cites fact IDs.
- **Agent 3 (verifier, rules plus `gpt-6-luna`):** checks citations, every number at the precision written, labels, quotes, and which series and markets are named. The model then judges whether the cited facts support each claim. A failing claim is sent back for one rewrite, and anything still failing is removed and shown in the report.
- **Frontend:** a single evaluation page. Colours, 3px buttons, the 84px navigation bar, the sticky section tabs and the key-figure rows are measured from bmw.de; content cards have rounder corners, as you chose. It uses the official BMW logo and BMW Type Next. The page also has the series × market matrix, the interactive graph, the verification report and the decision record. The old pages are deleted; their API endpoints remain.

**What I checked**
- **Tests:** 29 pass. They include a made-up number being stripped, a number hidden as "€3.9k" being caught, a wrong series or a misquote being caught, and a realistic 13-claim brief passing with nothing wrongly removed.
- **Browser:** I ran the app in a real browser at desktop and phone width, with no layout overflow and no page errors. The only console message is the expected "no key" response from the explanation step.
- **Not yet seen for real:** the explanation and verification sections were rendered with a faked server response, not real model output.

**Once you have the key**, put `OPENAI_API_KEY=...` in a `.env` file in the repo root (it's git-ignored), then run:
```
python -m bmw_feedback agent --check                 # which configured models your key can use
python -m bmw_feedback agent "Make seat massage standard on the 5 Series in Europe"
python -m bmw_feedback serve                         # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

The BMW logo and font are git-ignored and only on this machine. [fetch-brand-assets.cjs](frontend/scripts/fetch-brand-assets.cjs) downloads them again. Nothing is committed; the design spec is in [docs/superpowers/specs/](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-pm-idea-evaluator-design.md) and setup is in the [README](README.md). The main code is in [bmw_feedback/graph/](bmw_feedback/graph/), [bmw_feedback/agents/](bmw_feedback/agents/) and [IdeaEvaluation.tsx](frontend/src/pages/IdeaEvaluation.tsx).

The app is running at **http://127.0.0.1:8010**. A full evaluation ran against the real OpenAI API for the first time. I used the idea "Make seat massage standard on the 5 Series in Europe".

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Retriever (`gpt-6-luna`) | Chose "Seat massage", 5 Series (G60), Europe, move "make standard", and its answer passed validation on the first attempt. The semantic search used OpenAI embeddings. |
| Explainer | Wrote 18 claims in 15 seconds. |
| Verifier | All 18 claims verified, none removed, no rewrite needed. |

The brief says 'Consider', not 'Prioritise', for this idea. It also warns that the Europe complaint and request evidence is borrowed from other markets, and that the price list is German only.

**Two things you should know**
- **Explainer model:** `gpt-6-terra` isn't available to your key, but `gpt-5.6-terra` is, so I started the app with `OPENAI_EXPLAINER_MODEL=gpt-5.6-terra`. I did not change your `.env`.
